# Planned Ltd

> Planned Ltd is a UK project planning and controls consultancy for construction and infrastructure. Its services cover planning and scheduling (tender programmes, NEC4 first programmes and monthly updates, MS Project to P6 conversion, interim and retained planners); project controls and PMO support (cost, risk, reporting and earned value); delay and claims (extension of time and delay analysis, impacted programmes for compensation events, claims support); schedule assurance and reviews (NEC4 programme acceptance reviews, independent DCMA 14 point schedule assurance, migration readiness); and systems and training (Primavera P6 and Oracle Primavera Cloud administration, training and the Planned Academy). Sectors: construction, energy and utilities, transport and infrastructure, and Gulf projects under FIDIC.

Each engagement has a named lead, every deliverable is reviewed by a senior planner before issue, and a bench of senior planners and specialists provides extra capacity. Company number 08881845, registered in England and Wales. Cyber Essentials certified, APM Corporate Affiliate, Disability Confident Committed. Verifiable details are published at the credentials page below.

## Fixed scope reviews

- [NEC4 Programme Acceptance Review](https://plannedltd.co.uk/reviews/nec4-programme-acceptance-review): independent review of a contractor's programme against clause 31.2, with any recommendation for non-acceptance framed in the language of clause 31.3, delivered inside the contractual reply period.
- [Independent Schedule Assurance Review](https://plannedltd.co.uk/reviews/independent-schedule-assurance-review): full DCMA 14 point assessment plus logic quality and float integrity, with a scored verdict and a fix list.
- [Delay and EOT Position Review](https://plannedltd.co.uk/reviews/delay-and-eot-position-review): a candid assessment of the delay position before committing to a claim.
- [Primavera Migration Readiness Assessment](https://plannedltd.co.uk/reviews/primavera-cloud-migration-readiness-assessment): independent readiness assessment for organisations moving from Microsoft Project, Excel or another planning tool to Primavera P6 or Oracle Primavera Cloud: which platform fits, what converts, what to rebuild, standards and training.
- [All fixed scope reviews](https://plannedltd.co.uk/reviews/)

## Services

- [Tender programmes](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/tender-programmes): Primavera P6 programmes for bids and framework call-offs, built to the ITT and the client's specification, with a narrative, and set up to become the NEC clause 31 first programme if you win.
- [NEC first programme and monthly updates](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/nec-baseline-and-monthly-updates): the first programme for acceptance under NEC4 ECC or TSC, then kept current fortnightly or monthly in Primavera P6, with compensation event time effects where instructed.
- [Project planning and scheduling](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/project-planning): programmes built from the method and resources, taken through acceptance, kept current through delivery and recovered when they slip, for construction and infrastructure.
- [Project controls and PMO support](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/project-controls): progress measurement, earned value, change and early warning registers, reporting and dashboards, and supplier programme governance under NEC clauses 31 and 32.
- [Enabling and early works programmes](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/enabling-works-programmes): Primavera P6 programmes for utility diversions, site clearance, demolition, earthworks and temporary works, from tender programme to acceptance, monthly updates and compensation events.
- [Delay analysis and extension of time](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/delay-and-claims): NEC compensation event time assessment, extension of time claims under JCT and FIDIC, review of contractor claims for clients, and programme records, with the method chosen to fit the records.
- [Schedule risk analysis](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/risk-analysis): quantitative schedule risk analysis (QSRA) on a checked programme: duration ranges, risk mapping, Monte Carlo simulation, confidence levels on key dates and a contingency recommendation.
- [Resource loading and levelling](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/resource-management): programmes loaded from the method and levelled against available gangs, plant and specialists, with every moved date documented.
- [Primavera P6 administration](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/p6-administration): enterprise implementation, configuration, database consolidation, cloud migration, security and ongoing administration.
- [Oracle Primavera Cloud consultancy](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/oracle-primavera-cloud-consultant): OPC implementation, migration from P6 and team enablement.
- [Primavera P6 consultancy](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/primavera-p6-consultant): hands-on P6 planning and scheduling support.
- [Training](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/training): instructor-led Primavera P6 and Oracle Primavera Cloud courses from fundamentals to advanced, delivered remotely or on site.
- [MS Project to Primavera P6 conversion and programme rebuild](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/ms-project-to-p6-conversion): converting an MS Project construction programme into Primavera P6, and rebuilding a programme already in P6 to a client's planning specification: WBS, activity ID convention, activity codes, calendars, percent complete type, scheduling settings and reporting layouts, delivered as a native .xer, .xml or .plf with an ID mapping table and a DCMA-aligned quality check.
- [AI schedule assurance](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/ai-schedule-assurance): independent, human assurance of AI-generated and AI-assisted construction schedules, a DCMA 14 point and logic check against the client's specification, so the programme is sound, compliant and defensible before it is submitted.
- [Interim and retained planners](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services/interim-p6-planner): an independent Primavera P6 planner on your programme, embedded for a project or retained for a few days a month, building to NEC clause 31, running the monthly clause 32 updates and supporting recovery, without a permanent hire or your own P6 licence.
- [All services](https://plannedltd.co.uk/services)

## Free tools

- [Schedule Health Check](https://plannedltd.co.uk/tools/schedule-health-check): a free browser-based tool that runs the full DCMA 14 point assessment and returns an A to F grade with the failing activities named. It accepts Primavera P6 .xer, Primavera P6 XML and Microsoft Project XML files. It reports logic, leads, lags, relationship types, hard constraints, high float, negative float, high duration, invalid dates, resources, missed tasks, the critical path test, CPLI and BEI, and it marks any check it cannot compute from the file as not assessable rather than passing it silently. It also shows the total float distribution and traces the critical path. All analysis runs client-side and no file is uploaded to any server.

## Guides and reference

- [How to Get an NEC4 Programme Accepted First Time (Clause 31)](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/nec4-clause-31-programme-acceptance): The four grounds a Project Manager can use to reject an NEC4 programme, what clause 31.2 requires, and how to build one in P6 that is accepted first time.
- [How to Submit an NEC4 Revised Programme (Clause 32)](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/nec4-clause-32-revised-programme): What a clause 32 revision must show, when you have to submit one, and the two-minute P6 step that protects your compensation event assessment.
- [NEC4 Subcontractor Programme Obligations: A Practical Guide](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/nec4-subcontractor-programme-obligations): Your programme only protects you if it is in the Contractor's Accepted Programme. What to check, and why your compensation event clock runs on your own awareness.
- [Why Procurement Reform Won't Fix the Programme](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/the-programme-procurement-reform-forgot): The CMA's procurement diagnosis is right but stops short of the moment delay is decided: when a programme nobody tested is accepted.
- [A new delay date is not proof of a better plan](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/what-a-new-delay-date-proves): why a revised completion date says little about whether the programme behind it has actually been re-tested against its logic.
- [Oracle's new Primavera AI will not catch a bad schedule](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/primavera-unifier-ai-schedule-assurance): what Primavera Unifier's new AI agents do, what they do not check, and why independent schedule assurance still matters.
- [Project controls vs project management: who do you actually need?](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/project-controls-vs-project-management): the APM's seven-element definition, the NEC "Project Manager" distinction, and a decision framework by project size and contract form.
- [How to fix a broken P6 schedule: a step-by-step recovery plan](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/how-to-fix-a-broken-p6-schedule): diagnose, rebuild the logic, re-baseline with governance, and when to bring in outside help.
- [Who checks the schedule the AI wrote? AI schedule assurance explained](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/who-checks-the-schedule-the-ai-wrote)
- [The DCMA 14 point schedule assessment, explained](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/dcma-14-point-schedule-assessment)
- [How to read a DCMA 14-point check result in P6, without overreacting](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/dcma-14-point-check-triage): the P6 workflow for triaging a fail, what the built-in Check Schedule Report does and does not compute (it misses CPT and CPLI), and how to decide what needs fixing before a deadline.
- [The independent schedule review checklist: what a reviewer checks beyond DCMA](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/independent-schedule-review-checklist): seven checks a reviewer runs in Primavera P6 after a DCMA pass, with menu paths, covering calendars, WBS coverage, logic quality, constraints, resourcing, baseline resets and the critical path.
- [NEC4 programme requirements: what contractors need to know](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/nec4-programme-requirements)

- [EOT claims: why your records matter more than method](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/eot-claims-records-not-method): a forensic delay analysis is only as strong as the programme records behind it.
- [Schedule risk analysis: a practical guide for P6 planners](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/p6-schedule-risk-analysis)
- [Earned value management for construction projects](https://plannedltd.co.uk/blog/earned-value-management-construction)
